headline: No votes were taken; staff gave an update on CharacterStrong lessons, the bus behavior protocol, and the phone policy.
summary: No votes were taken. Staff gave an update on strategic initiatives 3.1 and 3.2, which cover school culture and climate. Topics included CharacterStrong social-emotional lessons, a new bus behavior response protocol, and the personal electronic device policy.
discussion: CharacterStrong implementation: Staff reported that lessons are running in all schools, with 2,256 hours logged and 82% at the Tier 1 level. Secondary schools are still working to blend the curriculum with existing school practices.

Bus behavior response protocol: Staff said drivers were trained last week on a protocol that matches school responses. Drivers report behavior on a form, and building administrators handle the follow-up.

Personal electronic device policy: Staff said entry-level logistics are going well, but headphones are still a problem in hallways. Early data shows about 89 violations by 74 students through October 23, and a full update is set for November 24.

Behavior screening and supports: Members asked how students are identified for behavior support. Staff described SWIS referral data, a screener, and Tier 2 supports that can start within about five days.

Parent engagement: Members asked how parents are involved in behavior protocols and the social-emotional curriculum, especially at the secondary level. Staff said they did not know of a curriculum requirement for parent involvement and would follow up.
